articoli.titolo: From 8,000 Spots to a World of Folks
articoli.estratto: The story behind SpotFolk: how a personal collection of places became an idea for a different kind of community.
articoli.testo:
It started with a map.

Over the years, I had collected more than 8,000 locations around the world. Places I had discovered through remote scouting, hours spent exploring satellite images, maps, travel blogs and geographical details, but also through personal experiences, road trips and time spent out in the field.

Some were hidden viewpoints, others forgotten villages, quiet roads, mountain trails, unusual architectural details or simply places that made me stop and look twice.

Each location had something that caught my attention. And gradually, the collection became something much bigger than a personal archive.

I called them *Spots*.

## An obsession with finding places

Finding interesting locations has always been part of the way I approach photography and travelling.

Sometimes, discovering a place starts long before actually getting there. I can spend hours exploring a remote area on a map, following a road that seems to lead nowhere, looking for an unusual coastline or trying to understand how the light might interact with a particular landscape.

Other times, a Spot comes from a completely different experience: a place I stumble upon while travelling, a recommendation from someone, or a location that surprises me when I least expect it.

Remote scouting and real-world exploration eventually became two sides of the same process.

The result was a growing collection of thousands of places, each with its own potential story.

At some point, I started thinking: why should all these discoveries remain mine?

## From my map to everyone's map

My first idea was quite simple: make the map public and allow other people to explore my collection.

I wanted to share those 8,000 Spots with photographers, travellers and curious people looking for somewhere different to go.

But the more I thought about it, the more I realised that simply opening my map wasn't enough.

There are millions of interesting places in the world, and no single person could ever discover them all.

What if other people could contribute their own discoveries?

What if a photographer could share a viewpoint, a hiker could add a trail, a traveller could recommend a little village, and someone passionate about food could introduce a place worth travelling for?

The map could become something that grows with its community.

Not just a collection of places, but a shared collection of discoveries.

And that changed everything.

## Then came the Folks

The next question was: who are the people behind these places?

Most platforms organise places around ratings, reviews and stars. You visit somewhere, leave a score, write a few lines and move on.

But I always felt something was missing.

A five-star rating doesn't tell me much about the person who gave it. It doesn't tell me what they were looking for, what caught their attention or why they decided that a particular place was worth sharing.

I wanted something more personal.

That's where the idea of the *Folk* came from.

Every user becomes a Folk. Every Spot can carry the signature of the person who discovered it or chose to share it.

A photographer, a hiker, a foodie, a traveller, a digital nomad: different people, different interests, different ways of looking at the world.

And each of them brings something unique to the map.

The interesting part is no longer just the place itself. It's the person behind the discovery.

## Less about stars. More about signatures.

I don't think places need another endless competition of ratings and reviews.

What makes a location interesting is often much more subjective than a number.

A hidden viewpoint might be extraordinary to a landscape photographer. A quiet mountain refuge might mean everything to a hiker. A tiny restaurant might become someone's favourite discovery of an entire journey.

None of these experiences needs to be validated by a five-star rating.

Sometimes, knowing who recommends a place is far more valuable than knowing how many stars it has.

That's the idea behind SpotFolk: **your signature makes the Spot worth discovering.**

Not because every recommendation has to be perfect, but because every discovery comes from a real person with their own perspective.

## A map that belongs to everyone

SpotFolk is still built around the original idea: discovering interesting places and making them easier to find.

But it has evolved into something more ambitious.

I started with more than 8,000 Spots collected over years of scouting and exploration. Today, I want to see that map grow through the eyes of thousands of different people.

I don't want it to be just my map anymore.

I want it to become a place where photographers, travellers, hikers, food lovers and curious minds can leave their mark, share what they find and discover the world through someone else's eyes.

Because the world doesn't need another list of the best places.

It needs more people willing to share the places they love.

And every Spot deserves a Folk behind it.

## Around the fire, there's room for you.

Every great journey is better when shared.

And every good story deserves an audience.

I imagine SpotFolk as a campfire somewhere in the world. A place where people with different backgrounds, passions and experiences gather to share the places they've discovered, the paths they've taken and the stories they've collected along the way.

Some come with photographs. Others with hiking trails, favourite food spots, hidden villages or simply a curiosity to explore.

It doesn't matter what kind of Folk you are. What matters is what you bring to the circle.

So, pull up a seat. There's room around the fire.

**Come join the Folks. Discover new places, share your own Spots and leave your signature on the map.**

The fire is already burning. We're just waiting for you.

**[Join SpotFolk → spotfolk.eu](https://spotfolk.eu)**
